source_text: 1. Icrrur secundum magnitudinem non est cognoscere Deum ; impossibile est enim mensurari Patrem ; secundum autem dilectionem ejus, hee est enim que nos per Verbum ejus perducit ad Deum, obedientes ei semper discimus quoniam est tantus Deus, et ipse est qui per semetipsum constituit, et elegit, et adornavit, qui est secundum nos. Et nos igitur cum his que continentur ab eo, factisumus. Et hic est de quo Scriptura ait; Ht plasmavit Deus hominem, limum terre accipiens, et insufflavit in faciem ejus Jjlatum vite. Non ergo angeli fecerunt, nos, nec nos plasmaverunt, nec angeli potuerunt imaginem facere Dei, nec alius quis preter Verbum Domini, nec virtus longe absistens a Patre uniNec enim indigebat horum Deus ad faciendum quie ipse apud se preefinierat fieri, quasi ipse suas non haberet manus. Adest enim ei semper Verbum et Sapientia, Filius et Spiritus, per quos, et in quibus omnia libere et sponte fecit, ad quos et loquitur, dicens: Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram; ipse a semetipso substantiam creaturarum, et exemplum factorum, et figuram in mundo ornamentorum accipiens. 2. Bene igitur pronuntiavit scriptura que dicit: Primo omnium crede, quoniam unus est Deus, qui omnia constituit, et consummavit, et fecit ex eo quod non erat, ut essent omnia: Omnium capax, et qui a nemine capiatur. Bene autem et in prophetis Malachias ait: Nonne unus Deus qui constituit nos? Nonne Pater unus est omnium nostrum ? Consequenter autem et Apostolus ait: nus Deus, inquit, Pater, qui super omnes, et in omnibus nobis. Similiter autem et Dominus: Omnia mihi, inquit, tradita sunt a Patre meo; manifeste ab eo qui omnia fecit: non enim aliena, sed In omnibus autem nihil subtractum est: et propter hoe idem est Judex viventium et mortuorum, habens clavem David: ' aperiet, et nemo claudet : claudet, et nemo aperiet. Nemo enim alius poterat nec in ccelo, nec in terra, nec sub terra aperire paternum librum, nec videre eum, nisi agnus qui occisus est, et sanguine suo redemit nos, ab eodem, qui omnia Verbo fecit et Sapientia adornavit, accipiens omnium potestatem, quando Verbum caro factum est, ut quemadmodum in ccelis principatum habuit Verbum Dei, sic et in terra haberet principatum, quoniam homo justus, gui peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus; principatum autem habeat eorum que sunt sub terra, ipse primogenitus mortuorum factus, et ut videant omnia, quemadmodum preediximus, suum Regem: et ut in carnem Domini occurrat paterna lux, et a carne ejus rutila veniat in nos, et sic homo deveniat in incorruptelam, circumdatus paterno lumine. 3. Et quoniam Verbum, id est Filius, semper cum Patre erat, per multa demonstravimus. Quoniam autem et Sapientia, est Spiritus, erat apud eum ante omnem constitutionem, per Salomonem ait: Deus sapientia fundavit terram, paravit Sensu ejus abyssi eruperunt, nubes autem manaverunt ros. Et rursus autem: Dominus creavit me principium viarum suarum in opera sua, ante swcula fundavit me, initio antequam terram faceret, priusqguam abyssos constitueret, et priusquam procederent fontes aquarum, antequam montes confirmarentur: ante omnes autem colles genuit me. Et iterum: Cum pararet coelum, eram cum illo,* et cum firmos faceret fontes abyssi, quando fortia faciebat fundamenta terra, eram apud eum aptans. Eyo eram cui adgaudebat, quotidie autem letabar ante faciem ejus in omni tempore, cum letaretur orbe perfecto, et jocundaretur in filiis hominum. 4. Unus igitur Deus, qui Verbo et Sapientia fecit et ° adaptavit omnia: hic est autem Demiurgus, qui et mundum hune attribuit humano generi, qui secundum magnitudinem quidem ignotus est omnibus his qui ab eo facti sunt: nemo enim investigavit altitudinem ejus, nec veterum qui quieverunt, nec eorum qui nune sunt, secundum autem dilectionem cognoscitur semper per eum, per quem constituit omnia. ejus Dominus noster Jesus Christus, qui novissimis temporibus homo in hominibus factus est, ut finem conjungeret principio, id Et propterea prophetee ab eodem Verbo proest, hominem Deo. pheticum accipientes charisma, preedicaverunt ejus secundum carnem adventum, per quem commixtio et communio Dei et hominis secundum placitum Patris facta est, ab initio preenunciante Verbo Dei, quoniam videbitur Deus ab hominibus, et conversabitur cum eis super terram, et colloqueretur, et adfuturus esset suo plasmati, salvans illud, et perceptibilis ab eo, et liberans nos de manibus omnium odientium nos, hoc est, ab universo transgressionis spiritu: et faciens nos servire sibi in sanctitate et Justitia omnes dies nostros, uti complexus homo Spiritum Dei, in gloriam cedat Patris. Hee prophetice significabant prophetze, sed non quemadmodum quidam dicunt, invisibili Patre omnium exsistente, alterum esse eum, qui a prophetis videretur.
pass_a_gloss: It is not possible to know God according to magnitude; for it is impossible to measure the Father; but according to his love, this is what leads us to God through his Word, always learning, obeying him, that God is so great, and he is the one who establishes, chooses, and adorns, who is according to us. And we, therefore, have been made with the things that are contained by him. And this is what Scripture says: God formed man, taking clay of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life. Therefore, angels did not make us, nor did they form us, nor could angels make the image of God, nor anyone else except the Word of the Lord, nor a power far removed from the Father. For God did not need these things to do what he had predetermined to do, as if he did not have his own hands. For the Word and Wisdom, the Son and Spirit, are always present with him, through whom, and in whom, he freely and willingly made all things, to whom he also speaks, saying: Let us make man in our image and likeness; he himself takes the substance of creatures, and the example of things made, and the form of ornaments in the world, from himself. Scripture has rightly declared, saying: First of all, believe that there is one God, who established, and consummated, and made all things from what did not exist, so that all things might be: capable of all, and not capable of being grasped by anyone. And in the prophets, Malachi says: Is there not one God who established us? Is there not one Father of us all? And the Apostle says: There is one God, the Father, who is over all, and in us all. And the Lord says: All things have been handed over to me by my Father; clearly by him who made all things: for they are not alien, but his own. And in all things, nothing has been subtracted: and because of this, he is the Judge of the living and the dead, having the key of David: he will open, and no one will shut: he will shut, and no one will open. For no one else could open the book of the Father, either in heaven, or on earth, or under the earth, except the Lamb who was slain, and redeemed us with his own blood, from him who made all things by the Word, and adorned them with Wisdom, receiving all power, when the Word became flesh, so that just as the Word of God had dominion in heaven, so also he might have dominion on earth, because the just man, who did not commit sin, and in whose mouth no deceit was found; and he might have dominion over the things that are under the earth, having become the firstborn of the dead, and so that all things might see their King, and the paternal light might shine forth in the flesh of the Lord, and the radiant light might come to us from his flesh, and so man might become incorrupt, surrounded by the paternal light.

pass_b_english: God cannot be known by measuring his magnitude; indeed, it is impossible to measure the Father. But according to his love, we are led to God through his Word. As we obey him, we learn continually just how great God is. He is the one who, in relation to us, establishes, chooses, and adorns. Therefore, we have been formed together with all things that are contained by him. This is the one of whom Scripture says: "God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Genesis 2:7). Consequently, angels did not make us, nor did they form us; angels could not fashion the image of God, nor could anyone else except the Word of the Lord—not a power standing far off from the Father. God had no need of such helpers to do what he had predetermined, as if he lacked his own hands. For the Word and Wisdom, the Son and Spirit, are always present with him. Through them and in them he freely and willingly made all things. He speaks to them, saying, "Let us make man in our image and likeness" (Genesis 1:26), while drawing the substance of creatures, the pattern of his works, and the form of the world's ornaments from himself.

Scripture has rightly declared: "First of all, believe that there is one God, who established, consummated, and made all things out of what did not exist, so that they might be—capable of all things, yet grasped by no one." Malachi also says well in the prophets: "Is there not one God who created us? Is there not one Father of us all?" (Malachi 2:10). The Apostle likewise affirms: "There is one God, the Father, who is over all and in all" (Ephesians 4:6). And the Lord himself says: "All things have been handed over to me by my Father" (Matthew 11:27)—clearly by the One who made all things, for they are not alien but his own. Nothing has been subtracted from his dominion; therefore he is the Judge of the living and the dead, holding the key of David: "He will open, and no one will shut; he will shut, and no one will open" (Revelation 3:7). No one else in heaven, on earth, or under the earth could open the Father's book or look upon it, except the Lamb who was slain. He redeemed us by his blood from the One who made all things by the Word and adorned them with Wisdom. When the Word became flesh, he received all authority, so that just as the Word of God held dominion in heaven, he might also hold dominion on earth—because he is the righteous man who committed no sin, in whose mouth no deceit was found (Isaiah 53:9; 1 Peter 2:22)—and dominion over those under the earth, having become the firstborn from the dead (Colossians 1:18). Thus all things might see their King, the paternal light might shine forth in the Lord's flesh, radiant light might come to us from his flesh, and humanity might become incorruptible, clothed in the Father's light.

We have shown through many proofs that the Word, that is, the Son, was always with the Father. That Wisdom is the Spirit, present with him before any creation, Solomon declares: "By wisdom the Lord founded the earth; by understanding he established the heavens. By his knowledge the deeps broke open, and the clouds dropped down dew" (Proverbs 3:19–20). And again: "The Lord created me at the beginning of his work, the first of his acts of old. Ages ago I was set up, at the first, before the beginning of the earth. When there were no depths I was brought forth, before the springs of water, before the mountains were shaped, before the hills, I was brought forth" (Proverbs 8:22–25). And again: "When he established the heavens, I was there; when he made firm the fountains of the deep, when he established the foundations of the earth, I was beside him, like a master workman. I was daily his delight, rejoicing before him always, rejoicing in his inhabited world and delighting in the children of man" (Proverbs 8:27–31).

Therefore there is one God, who by the Word and Wisdom made and ordered all things. He is the Artificer who gave this world to the human race. In his magnitude he is unknown to all who were made by him; no one has searched out his height—neither the ancients who have rested nor those who live now. But according to his love, he is known always through the One by whom he established all things: our Lord Jesus Christ. In these last times he became a man among men, to join the end to the beginning. For this reason the prophets, receiving the prophetic gift from the same Word, proclaimed his coming in the flesh, through whom the mingling and communion of God and man came about according to the Father's good pleasure. From the beginning the Word of God foretold that God would be seen by men, would dwell with them on earth, would speak with them, and would be present to his creation—saving it, making it capable of perceiving him, and freeing us from the hands of all who hate us, that is, from the whole spirit of transgression—so that we might serve him in holiness and righteousness all our days (Luke 1:74–75), and that humanity, embracing the Spirit of God, might pass into the glory of the Father. The prophets signified these things prophetically, but not as some claim: that because the Father of all is invisible, the one seen by the prophets was a different God.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful clause-by-clause translation. Pass B provides a more fluent version with necessary scripture citations (Genesis 2:7, Genesis 1:26, Malachi 2:10, Ephesians 4:6, Matthew 11:27, Revelation 3:7, Isaiah 53:9, 1 Peter 2:22, Colossians 1:18, Proverbs 3:19-20, Proverbs 8:22-25, Proverbs 8:27-31, Luke 1:74-75) which are required for the scriptural allusions present in the Latin. The title 'Knowledge of God' correctly names the thought of the passage.
